extracted.intended_audience: Authors and conductors of systematic reviews of interventions (Cochrane reviewers, meta-analysts, health researchers, guideline developers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, conducting, analysing, reporting, and maintaining Cochrane systematic reviews of interventions, including methods for searching, selection, bias assessment, meta-analysis, and presenting findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing a Cochrane review
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the initial steps and overall preparation required to produce a Cochrane review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter in the Cochrane Handbook; likely covers planning, team roles, timelines, registry/protocol preparation and administrative steps. (Catalog page lists the chapter title but does not reproduce chapter text.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining reviews : updates, amendments, and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and procedures for keeping reviews current, incorporating amendments, and responding to feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses how and when to update reviews, how to handle protocol/amendment changes, and processes for receiving/responding to feedback; detailed policies are contained in the handbook chapter itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide to the contents of a Cochrane protocol and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification of the required sections and items that must appear in a Cochrane protocol and the final review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines expected structure and mandatory content (e.g., background, objectives, methods, outcomes) for protocols and reviews; full item-level guidance available in the handbook chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining the review question and developing criteria for including studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and processes for formulating a clear review question and explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (population, intervention, comparator, outcomes, study designs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers how to define scope, PICO elements, eligibility criteria and rationale; the catalog only lists the chapter heading, not the full guidance text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching for studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods and standards for designing and executing literature searches to identify all relevant studies for the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes database selection, search strategy design, grey literature searching, documenting searches, and dealing with language/publication bias; detailed search methods and examples are in the handbook chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting studies and collecting data
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes for screening studies against inclusion criteria and extracting/storing required data from included studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers dual screening, data extraction forms, dealing with discrepancies, contacting authors, and data management best practices; refer to chapter for templates and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing risk of bias in included studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and tools for evaluating internal validity and risk of bias of studies included in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likely describes Cochrane's risk of bias domains (randomization, allocation concealment, blinding, incomplete outcome data, selective reporting, other biases), judgement rules, and presentation; full tool and guidance found in the handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysing data and undertaking meta-analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on statistical analysis methods, pooling data, model selection, heterogeneity assessment, and sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers fixed/random effects models, dealing with different outcome measures, subgroup and meta-regression analyses, and statistical assumptions; chapter contains worked examples and technical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing reporting biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods to detect and mitigate biases arising from selective reporting and publication bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes funnel plots, tests for small-study effects, consideration of outcome reporting bias, and strategies for reducing their impact on conclusions; handbook chapter contains procedures and interpretation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presenting results and "summary of findings" tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for how to present review results clearly, including construction and use of Summary of Findings (SoF) tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes what to include in SoF tables (outcomes, effect estimates, certainty of evidence), formatting, and explanatory text; actual templates and explanatory guidance are in the handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting results and drawing conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for interpreting the evidence, considering certainty, applicability, and making balanced conclusions and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses strength of evidence, clinical importance vs statistical significance, limitations, implications for practice and research; see chapter for frameworks and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including non-randomized studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when and how to include and appraise non-randomized studies of interventions in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers eligibility, risk of bias considerations specific to observational designs, synthesis approaches, and cautions about causal inference; detailed methods in the handbook chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for identifying, extracting, analysing, and reporting harms and adverse effects related to interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes search strategies for harms, handling sparse/unsystematic harms data, classification and presentation of adverse events; full methodological detail found in the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporating economics evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches for identifying, appraising, and integrating economic/economic-evidence (cost-effectiveness) information into reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers types of economic evidence, methods for summarising costs and resource use, and principles for incorporating economics into decision-relevant summaries; see handbook chapter for examples and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special topics in statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced statistical issues and specialized methods relevant to meta-analysis and data synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likely addresses issues such as complex data structures, multi-arm trials, rare events, and advanced modelling techniques; detailed statistical treatments are in the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient-reported outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on using, analysing, and presenting patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) in systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers selection of PROMs, interpretation of scores, pooling methods for different instruments, and considerations for measurement validity and responsiveness; chapter provides examples and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews of individual patient data
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for conducting reviews and meta-analyses using individual participant (patient-level) data (IPD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes IPD collection processes, data harmonization, one-stage vs two-stage analyses, and benefits/limitations of IPD meta-analysis; comprehensive guidance in the handbook chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods and considerations for planning and conducting prospective meta-analyses (studies planned and pooled prospectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses protocol coordination, data collection harmonization, pre-specification of analyses, and governance issues; chapter contains procedural recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative research and Cochrane reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches for locating, appraising, and incorporating qualitative research into Cochrane reviews to address questions such as acceptability and implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers qualitative synthesis methods, when qualitative evidence is appropriate, and how to integrate qualitative findings with quantitative evidence; detailed methods in the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews in health promotion and public health
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological considerations specific to reviews of public health and health-promotion interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes challenges such as complex interventions, context dependence, policy-level outcomes, and broader study designs; chapter provides tailored guidance and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overviews of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for conducting overviews (reviews of systematic reviews), including synthesis, overlap handling, and appraisal of included reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses scope definition, mapping of evidence, assessment of review quality, dealing with overlapping primary studies, and presenting synthesized conclusions; see handbook chapter for protocols and methods.
